requirement: Identify the public pair as NCT03606928, mFLOT Chemotherapy as First-line Treatment in GC: a three-page protocol and separate one-page statistical-analysis document, both internally dated 2 May 2018; keep the reference document annotation-only and obtain second-review confirmation of the unsigned, unversioned prospective governing chain.

evidence.text: The protocol prints the title, NCT03606928 and Date: 2018/05/02.
The separate statistical-analysis page prints the same title, NCT and date.

notes: Both internal dates precede actual start, but neither PDF has a version, signature or approval trail and the registry was first submitted after start.

requirement: Describe the study as a single-arm modified-FLOT dose-escalation investigation in Chinese patients with metastatic gastric cancer using a classical 3+3 design; do not invent randomization or a concurrent control group.

evidence.text: The eligibility section identifies Chinese patients with metastatic gastric cancer and the treatment section specifies a classical 3+3 design.

requirement: Use the frozen protocol population: age 18-75 years, histologically confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma, untreated metastatic disease or recurrence more than six months after adjuvant chemotherapy, ECOG 0-2, life expectancy over three months and adequate hematologic, hepatic, renal and coagulation function; reconcile later registry eligibility before freeze rather than silently substituting it.
acceptable_values: untreated metastatic or recurrence over six months

evidence.text: The patient-eligibility paragraph supplies diagnosis, prior-treatment interval, age, ECOG 0-2, life expectancy and organ-function requirements.

notes: The later registry shows ECOG 0-1 and hemoglobin at least 90 g/L, versus protocol ECOG 0-2 and hemoglobin at least 75 g/L.

requirement: Apply the protocol exclusions for second primary malignancy, central nervous system metastasis, peripheral nerve disease, uncontrolled medical illness, contraindication or hypersensitivity to a study drug, and pregnancy.

evidence.text: The eligibility paragraph explicitly lists these exclusions.

requirement: Implement the classical 3+3 decision rule at each dose level: enroll at least three participants; escalate after zero DLTs; expand to six after one DLT among three; and declare the level intolerable when at least two of three or two of six participants experience DLT.
acceptable_values: at least three per dose level
one of three DLT expand to six
at least two of three or two of six DLT

evidence.text: The treatment plan gives the cohort size and zero-, one- and at-least-two-DLT escalation rules.

requirement: Start dose escalation at docetaxel 40 mg/m2 and oxaliplatin 65 mg/m2 and do not invent later dose levels or a complete escalation grid because the protocol-referenced Table 1 is absent from the frozen three-page PDF.

evidence.text: The treatment plan identifies both level-1 starting doses and says the escalation plan is listed in Table 1, which is not present in the supplied PDF.

requirement: Keep leucovorin fixed at 200 mg/m2 and 5-FU fixed at 2200 mg/m2 by 48-hour continuous infusion, administer treatment every two weeks and stop at progression, unacceptable toxicity, participant refusal or a maximum of 12 cycles.

evidence.text: The treatment paragraph fixes leucovorin and 5-FU doses and states the two-week schedule and stopping conditions.

requirement: For participants with stable disease or better after eight cycles, record whether they receive S-1 maintenance or four additional intravenous cycles and treat that physician-participant decision as an intercurrent treatment choice requiring prespecified analysis handling.
acceptable_values: stable disease or better after eight cycles

evidence.text: The protocol permits S-1 maintenance or four more intravenous cycles after SD or better at cycle 8, jointly decided by physicians and participants.

requirement: Apply no routine dose modification during cycles 1-2 unless a severe adverse event occurs; after cycle 2, reduce docetaxel, oxaliplatin and fluorouracil once by 20% after treatment-related grade 3-4 toxicity and omit the causative drug if grade 3-4 toxicity recurs after reduction.
acceptable_values: omit causative drug after recurrent grade 3-4 toxicity

evidence.text: The dose-modification paragraph supplies the timing, 20% reduction, one-reduction limit and subsequent drug-exclusion rule.

requirement: Require absolute granulocyte count at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelets at least 100 x 10^9/L and resolution of treatment-related toxicities to grade 1 or lower before starting the next treatment.
acceptable_values: toxicity resolved to grade 1 or lower

evidence.text: The protocol states all three restart criteria after its dose-reduction rules.

requirement: Define the DLT evaluation window as the first two treatment cycles and count febrile neutropenia, grade 4 neutropenia, grade 4 thrombocytopenia, grade 3 or higher infection, grade 3 or higher nonhematologic toxicity, or treatment delay of at least two weeks as DLT.

evidence.text: The toxicity section defines the first-two-cycle window and enumerates the DLT criteria.

requirement: Treat determination of maximum tolerated dose and recommended dose as the primary objective: MTD is the dose level at which at least two of three or two of six participants have DLT, and RD is the dose level below the MTD.
acceptable_values: at least two of three or two of six DLT
RD one dose level below MTD

evidence.text: The treatment plan defines MTD and RD from the 3+3 decisions.
The statistical-analysis page identifies MTD and RD as the primary endpoint.

requirement: Before finalization, define the dose-level DLT-evaluable set, all-treated safety set and response- and time-to-event-evaluable sets, including handling of ineligible participants, participants not completing the DLT window for non-DLT reasons, treatment delay, replacement, dose reduction, maintenance and early withdrawal.

evidence.text: The protocol defines eligibility, dose escalation, treatment modification and assessments but neither document defines analysis populations or replacement rules.

requirement: Define response rate as a RECIST 1.1 response outcome with the exact response categories, numerator, denominator, confirmation requirement and assessment window; report the estimate with an exact confidence interval rather than only a percentage.

evidence.text: The protocol classifies response under RECIST 1.1 and schedules imaging but does not operationalize RR.
The statistical-analysis page lists RR as secondary without a derivation or inferential rule.

requirement: Measure PFS from treatment start to the earliest documented disease progression or death from any cause, with chest, abdomen and pelvis CT at baseline within one week before treatment and every eight weeks irrespective of treatment delay, permitting symptom-triggered earlier imaging.
acceptable_values: progression or death from any cause

evidence.text: The response section gives the PFS origin/event definition and CT schedule, including early imaging for progression symptoms.

requirement: Estimate the PFS distribution by Kaplan-Meier and before freeze specify censoring for no event, no adequate post-baseline assessment, new anticancer treatment, missed assessments, loss to follow-up and database cutoff, together with medians, time-point estimates and two-sided confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The statistical-analysis page specifies Kaplan-Meier for PFS but no censoring, summary-time or interval rules.
The protocol supplies the progression/death event definition and imaging schedule only.

requirement: Retain overall survival as protocol-defined time from diagnosis to death from any cause, but confirm its hierarchy, analysis set, censoring date and reporting method because the one-page reference does not list OS among its secondary endpoints.

evidence.text: The protocol defines OS from diagnosis to death from any cause.
The reference names RR, PFS and safety as secondary endpoints and is silent on OS.

requirement: Define an estimand for each non-DLT efficacy endpoint, including population, endpoint, summary measure and handling of progression, death, dose reduction, omission of a causative drug, treatment discontinuation, S-1 maintenance, additional intravenous cycles and subsequent anticancer therapy.

evidence.text: The protocol permits dose changes, stopping and post-cycle-8 maintenance choices and defines efficacy outcomes without mapping those events to estimands.

requirement: Specify handling of missing or unevaluable DLT status, missing or off-schedule tumor assessments, incomplete RECIST response, missing event dates, withdrawal and loss to follow-up; distinguish endpoint derivation rules from sensitivity analyses for informative missingness.

evidence.text: The design includes DLT windows, treatment delay, repeated imaging and discontinuation, but neither source defines missing-data handling.

requirement: Analyze safety in all treated participants using NCI-CTCAE version 4.0, with weekly assessment during cycles 1-2 and every two weeks thereafter; summarize participants and events by dose level, system organ class, preferred term, maximum grade, seriousness, relationship, DLT status, dose modification, discontinuation and death.

evidence.text: The toxicity section specifies CTCAE v4.0 and the assessment frequency, while the treatment section defines toxicity-driven modifications.
Safety is a secondary endpoint, but the reference gives no summary structure.

requirement: Provide transparent descriptive summaries by dose level for disposition, eligibility, demographics, baseline disease, prior therapy, treatment exposure, relative dose intensity, delays, reductions, omitted drugs, maintenance and follow-up, using explicit denominators and no unsupported baseline significance tests.

evidence.text: The protocol defines eligibility, dose levels, treatment exposure and follow-up-relevant events, but neither document specifies descriptive outputs.

requirement: State that the selected PDFs provide no formal total sample-size, power or precision calculation and that accrual follows the 3+3 cohorts; do not use the later registry actual enrollment of 18 as a prospective target, and confirm any expansion-stage sample size before freeze.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies at least three participants per dose level and the 3+3 expansion rule but no total target or formal calculation.

requirement: Keep the MTD/RD decision separate from exploratory RR, PFS, OS and safety estimation and define any hierarchy, confidence levels and multiplicity labeling; do not claim confirmatory efficacy from this small uncontrolled dose-escalation study.
acceptable_values: RR PFS OS safety separately labeled

evidence.text: The reference names MTD/RD primary and RR, PFS and safety secondary but supplies no hierarchy or multiplicity rule.
The protocol additionally defines OS, creating an unresolved endpoint inventory.

requirement: Use SPSS version 22.0 if reproducing the reference analysis and before freeze specify reproducible code or procedures, validated software environment, two-sided confidence levels, exact small-sample methods, data-cutoff rules, listings and independent quality control; leave unresolved choices explicit.

evidence.text: The reference names SPSS version 22.0 but provides no confidence level, implementation, validation or quality-control details.
